title.en: Linking words: and, but, because, so, when
title.sl: Povezovalne besede: and, but, because, so, when
title.de: Bindewörter: and, but, because, so, when
title.it: Le congiunzioni: and, but, because, so, when

rule.sl:
Tri majhne besede povezujejo: **and** (in: še nekaj), **but** (ampak: nasprotje), **or** (ali: izbira): **We had soup and bread.** **Jack was tired, but he was happy.** **Tea or coffee?** Pred **but** je navadno vejica.

**because** (ker) pove razlog, **so** (zato) posledico: **We stayed at home because it rained.** (Ostali smo doma, ker je deževalo.) **It rained, so we stayed at home.** (Deževalo je, zato smo ostali doma.) Pred **so** je vejica. Pravi stavek ima samo eno od obeh: nikoli *Because it rained, so we stayed*.

Na **Why?** (zakaj?) odgovoriš z **because**: **Why did you stay? — Because it rained.** Stavek se lahko z njim začne: **Because it rained, we stayed at home.** V govoru je **because** pogosto *cos*.

**when** (ko), **before** (preden) in **after** (potem ko) povedo, kdaj: **When I got home, it was dark.** **Before I went to bed, I shut the door.** **After we ate, we washed up.** Če je ta del na začetku, je vejica; če je na koncu, je ni: **I shut the door before I went to bed.**

**then** (potem) pove, kaj je bilo naslednje: **We had dinner. Then we went home.** **We had dinner and then we went home.** Za **then** ni vejice.
rule.de:
Drei kleine Wörter: **and** (und: noch etwas), **but** (aber: das Gegenteil), **or** (oder: eine Wahl): **We had soup and bread.** **Jack was tired, but he was happy.** **Tea or coffee?** Vor **but** steht meist ein Komma.

**because** (weil) nennt den Grund, **so** (also) die Folge: **We stayed at home because it rained.** (Wir blieben zu Hause, weil es regnete.) **It rained, so we stayed at home.** Vor **so** steht ein Komma. Ein echter Satz hat nur eines von beiden: nie *Because it rained, so we stayed*. Nach because bleibt die Wortstellung normal, anders als nach weil.

Auf **Why?** (warum?) antwortest du mit **because**: **Why did you stay? — Because it rained.** Auch ein Satz kann damit beginnen: **Because it rained, we stayed at home.** Gesprochen ist **because** oft *cos*.

**when** (als), **before** (bevor) und **after** (nachdem) sagen, wann: **When I got home, it was dark.** **Before I went to bed, I shut the door.** **After we ate, we washed up.** Steht dieser Teil vorn, kommt ein Komma; steht er hinten, keines: **I shut the door before I went to bed.**

**then** (dann) sagt, was als Nächstes kam: **We had dinner. Then we went home.** Nach **then** kein Komma.
rule.it:
Tre piccole parole collegano: **and** (e: ancora qualcosa), **but** (ma: il contrario), **or** (o: una scelta): **We had soup and bread.** **Jack was tired, but he was happy.** **Tea or coffee?** Prima di **but** di solito c'è la virgola.

**because** (perché) dà il motivo, **so** (quindi) il risultato: **We stayed at home because it rained.** (Siamo rimasti a casa perché pioveva.) **It rained, so we stayed at home.** Prima di **so** c'è la virgola. Una frase vera ne ha uno solo: mai *Because it rained, so we stayed*.

A **Why?** (perché?) rispondi con **because**: l'italiano ha una parola sola, l'inglese due: **Why did you stay? — Because it rained.** Anche una frase può cominciare così: **Because it rained, we stayed at home.** A voce **because** spesso è *cos*.

**when** (quando), **before** (prima di) e **after** (dopo) dicono quando: **When I got home, it was dark.** **Before I went to bed, I shut the door.** **After we ate, we washed up.** Se questa parte viene prima, c'è la virgola; se viene dopo, no: **I shut the door before I went to bed.**

**then** (poi) dice che cosa è venuto dopo: **We had dinner. Then we went home.** Dopo **then** niente virgola.
rule.en:
Three small words join things: **and** (one more), **but** (the opposite), **or** (a choice): **We had soup and bread.** **Jack was tired, but he was happy.** **Tea or coffee?** A comma usually comes before **but**.

**because** gives the reason, **so** the result: **We stayed at home because it rained.** **It rained, so we stayed at home.** A comma comes before **so**. A real sentence takes one of them: never *Because it rained, so we stayed*.

**Why?** is answered with **because**: **Why did you stay? — Because it rained.** A sentence can open with it: **Because it rained, we stayed at home.** Spoken, **because** is often *cos*.

**when**, **before** and **after** say when: **When I got home, it was dark.** **Before I went to bed, I shut the door.** **After we ate, we washed up.** If this part comes first, put a comma; if it comes second, none: **I shut the door before I went to bed.**

**then** says what came next: **We had dinner. Then we went home.** **We had dinner and then we went home.** No comma after **then**.

rule.sl: **because: razlog. so: posledica.** En stavek, ena beseda: **We stayed because it rained.** **It rained, so we stayed.** **before**, **after**, **when** na začetku: vejica.
rule.de: **because: der Grund. so: die Folge.** Ein Satz, ein Wort: **We stayed because it rained.** **It rained, so we stayed.** **before**, **after**, **when** vorn: Komma.
rule.it: **because: il motivo. so: il risultato.** Una frase, una parola: **We stayed because it rained.** **It rained, so we stayed.** **before**, **after**, **when** all'inizio: virgola.
rule.en: **because: the reason. so: the result.** One sentence, one of them: **We stayed because it rained.** **It rained, so we stayed.** **before**, **after**, **when** first: a comma.

tip.sl: 💡 Nikoli **because** in **so** v istem stavku: **Because it rained, we stayed.**, nikoli *Because it rained, so we stayed*.
tip.de: 💡 Nie **because** und **so** in einem Satz: **Because it rained, we stayed.**, nie *Because it rained, so we stayed*.
tip.it: 💡 Mai **because** e **so** nella stessa frase: **Because it rained, we stayed.**, mai *Because it rained, so we stayed*.
tip.en: 💡 Never **because** and **so** in one sentence: **Because it rained, we stayed.**, never *Because it rained, so we stayed*.
